sources.title: Guidelines for Embedding Metadata in Broadcast WAVE Files
sources.version_or_commit: FADGI Audio-Visual Working Group, Version 3, approved 2021-04-26
sources.locator: PDF pp. 2–3 change list; pp. 6–10 bext fields; pp. 19–21 INFO; p. 26 CSET/code page
sources.observed_operation: web search/open; PDF parsed as text; locator lines included p.0–p.26
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BEXT Originator/OriginatorReference/Description are strongly recommended, with bounded lengths; OriginationDate is applied as file creation date and local archival timezone; INFO fields have individual recommended/optional labels. CSET is optional; absent or zero defaults to ISO 8859/1 for internal metadata text.
sources.applicability: Direct guidance for any optional BWF embedding; not a mandate to modify volunteer originals or adopt all fields.
sources.limitations: Guideline is 2021; it does not establish support in every recorder/player.

sources.title: Broadcast WAVE Audio File Format, Version 1 (Library of Congress Sustainability of Digital Formats)
sources.locator: Description and file structure; Sustainability factors; Self-documentation and accessibility notes; LC experience/preference
sources.observed_operation: web search/open; lines 52–65 and result text
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: BWF is WAVE plus required bext; ordinary WAV-capable software may render audio without exposing BWF metadata; embedded ltxt transcription text is not necessarily structured or screen-reader tagged.
sources.applicability: Explains tradeoffs between embedded BWF fields, general playback, and separate accessible transcript.
sources.limitations: LoC practice and preferences are reference points, not binding requirements for this society.

sources.title: BWF MetaEdit README
sources.version_or_commit: Repository master README, version not pinned by observed page; retrieved 2026-10-10
sources.locator: Feature list: import/edit/embed/export, validate, audio-only MD5 on WAVE data chunk
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Tool functions apply to WAVE/BWF files it can read; its MD5 feature is explicitly for the data chunk/audio bitstream, not a full-file digest.
sources.applicability: Candidate for staff-only optional metadata enrichment/validation on a copy; supports a separate audio-bitstream check.
sources.limitations: README is on a mutable branch; no local install or behavior test was performed.

sources.title: BWF MetaEdit GUI release history
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: 23.04 added read/write support for listed legacy code pages and CSET; 25.04 added ISO8859-1 fallback when reading core files. These are tool-specific release notes, not a promise of cross-tool round-trip.
sources.applicability: Evidence that encoding handling changed across releases and must be version-pinned/tested in this workflow.
sources.limitations: No actual BWF file was tested; historical release notes do not establish current installed version.

sources.title: BWF MetaEdit issue #29: non 7-bit ASCII
sources.version_or_commit: Issue opened 2017-10-18; closed issue; no release/commit relationship confirmed
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Reporter described open/close quotation bytes 0x93/0x94 that did not translate well; condition concerns non-7-bit ASCII data. The issue is evidence of a reported failure, not a general guarantee that current versions fail or are fixed.
sources.applicability: Illustrates punctuation/legacy-encoding risk for names, notes and embedded metadata round-trips.
sources.limitations: No tested resolution was tied to this issue during research.

sources.title: RFC 8493 — The BagIt File Packaging Format (V1.0)
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Bag MUST include data/ and at least one payload manifest; manifest lists every payload path and checksum; payload is treated as opaque octets for verification. Tag files use declared character encoding; bagit.txt UTF-8 without BOM.
sources.applicability: Portable, format-agnostic transfer envelope for audio, photos, notes, transcripts and access copies.
sources.limitations: Checksums establish integrity relative to the manifest, not descriptive truth, permission, redundancy or future preservation by themselves.

sources.title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata, Version 3.0
sources.version_or_commit: PREMIS Data Dictionary v3.0, published/updated November 2015
sources.locator: Official version landing page; hierarchical semantic units 1.13 relationships, 2.1–2.7 Event, 3 Agent; PDF pp. 28, 128, 151–166
sources.observed_operation: web search/open; official landing page, hierarchy and PDF parsed
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: PREMIS models Objects, Events, Rights and Agents; events carry identifier/type/date-time and can link agents and objects; relationships include derivation/structural types.
sources.applicability: Optional pattern for transcript revisions, derivation links and operator/tool/date/outcome logs; can be simplified for pilot.
sources.limitations: Full PREMIS implementation may be disproportionate; used here as a conceptual model, not a required schema.

sources.title: Transcribing Interviews — Veterans History Project, Library of Congress
sources.version_or_commit: Current unversioned guidance page as retrieved 2026-10-10
sources.locator: Search result sections: transcript/recording relationship and transcript editing tips
sources.observed_operation: web search returned page text; direct open returned HTTP 403, so content was not independently line-inspected
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: VHP says audio and transcript are complementary, not substitutes; transcripts are welcome but not required; identify transcriber/editor/date and clearly indicate transcript differences.
sources.applicability: Oral-history-specific support for optional transcript, separate revisions and provenance notes.
sources.limitations: Direct retrieval was blocked; use as supporting discovery only, corroborated by W3C accessibility guidance and the supplied brief for interviewer approval.

sources.title: Making Audio and Video Media Accessible — W3C WAI
sources.version_or_commit: W3C WAI resource first published 2019; updated 2024-09-17
sources.locator: Sections on transcripts and media players, lines 88–110
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAI recommends a transcript for speech and non-speech audio and an accessible media player; accessibility needs depend on the content/audience.
sources.applicability: Supports separate transcript and listening interface checks; does not define a preservation format or require a particular codec.
sources.limitations: General web accessibility guidance; local audience and consent policy remain owner inputs.

sources.title: Oral History Resources / OHMS — University of Kentucky Libraries Nunn Center
sources.version_or_commit: Current official resource page, unversioned; retrieved 2026-10-10
sources.observed_operation: web search retrieved official UK Libraries page
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: OHMS connects word-level search to interview moments; the page points to a free account and tool resources.
sources.applicability: Useful unfamiliar oral-history access approach; possible later pilot access layer.
sources.limitations: Describes access/discovery, not package-level preservation or local consent policy.

sources.title: OHMS Viewer repository and releases
sources.version_or_commit: Latest observed release tag v3.10.16, commit 3343b78; README also gives installation/customization instructions
sources.locator: Release page; repository README requirements and basic installation/test instructions
sources.observed_operation: web open/search on official University of Kentucky Libraries GitHub repository
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Viewer is a hosted PHP web app; installation requires web-server file access. Repository guidance calls for checking transcript/index searching and timepoint links after changing players.
sources.applicability: Evidence that OHMS has a hosting/customization burden and that player/media linkage needs testing.
sources.limitations: Observed release/version and README are not proof of compatibility with the society's files or server; no installation attempted.

sources.title: Digital Preservation at the Library of Congress
sources.locator: Tools and Open Source Software, lines 30–39
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: LoC describes BagIt as an IETF packaging specification, Bagger as an open-source BagIt packaging application, and BWF MetaEdit as embedding/validating/exporting metadata in BWF.
sources.applicability: Confirms concrete freely available tools associated with the two workflows.
sources.limitations: Tool listing is not an endorsement for this particular collection or a validation report.

sources.title: WAVE Audio File Format — Library of Congress Sustainability of Digital Formats
sources.locator: Identification/description and codec-dependent fidelity; extension/format identifiers
sources.observed_operation: web search; official FDD page text retrieved
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAVE is a wrapper that can contain different audio bitstreams; fidelity varies by selected codec. The .wav filename extension is one signifier, not the full codec identity.
sources.applicability: Supports inspection of actual format/codec before proposing copy/transcode or lossless claims.
sources.limitations: Format reference, not validation of any submitted file.

sources.title: Recommended Formats Statement — Audio Works, Library of Congress
sources.version_or_commit: Current audio recommendations as accessed 2026-10-10; 2025–2026 statement is also linked on the page
sources.locator: Section IV, ii. Audio — Media-independent (digital), format preferences
sources.observed_operation: web search on official LoC page
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: For media-independent digital audio, LoC prefers native/high-resolution and uncompressed options and ranks WAVE with embedded BWF metadata above WAVE without embedded metadata.
sources.applicability: A preservation-format reference for optional access/derivative choices; not a reason to reject varied volunteer submissions or alter them.
sources.limitations: LoC collection preference, not society-specific policy; source content categories and submission context differ.
